correctness.rationale: For every odd \(n\ge3\), lifting length-two walks establishes pairwise neighborhood intersections of size 0 or 2, so high-dimensional faces have unique facets and can be elementary-collapsed by explicit descending free-face pairs. The cubical two-skeleton of \(Q_n\) is simply connected, its free antipodal quotient corresponds to the four-cycle-filled graph complex \(X_2(FQ_n)\), and an odd deck-transformation path shows that its even-length fundamental subgroup is trivial. Matsushita 2017 Theorem 1.1 therefore yields \(\pi_1(\mathcal N(FQ_n))=0\); connectivity follows from the projected odd cycle. Exact face counts yield \(\chi=2^{n-3}(n^2-5n+8)\). Two-dimensionality, Hurewicz, and the homology Whitehead theorem prove the integral wedge decomposition, not just homology. Standalone explicit-collapse/face-count program and independent quotient-graph program checked \(n=3,5,7\) (and face numbers at \(n=9\)). Limits: finite programs do not prove the infinite statement; the all-n proof is mathematical, and independent validation remains absent.

value.rationale: This determines a complete integral homotopy invariant uniformly for a canonical infinite four-chromatic family of antipodal quotients of hypercube graphs, including the Clebsch graph and arbitrarily large folded cubes. The substantial feature is dimension compression from \(n-1\) to \(2\) plus a precise nontrivial sphere multiplicity \(2^{n-3}(n^2-5n+8)-1\); this is not implied by graph vertex/edge counts or the general fundamental-group theorem alone. It gives natural examples where the Lovasz obstruction is sharp, a novel uniform square-complex covering argument, and self-contained structural collapse steps, not arbitrary numerical slices. The proof does not assert an equivariant splitting or even-n case.
